measures.title: REQUIRE PHOTO ID FOR VOTING
measures.official_name: Require Photo ID for All Voters

measures.question: Constitutional amendment to require all voters, not just those presenting to vote in person, to present photo identification before voting.

measures.cost_note: The General Assembly lists no fiscal note from its Fiscal Research Division for Senate Bill 921 (Session Law 2024-58).

sections.heading: Official summary explanation
sections.by: Official summary explanation, prepared by the Legislative Services Officer of the North Carolina General Assembly under N.C.G.S. 147-54.10, adopted August 20, 2026
paragraphs: This amendment to the North Carolina Constitution would require presentation of photographic identification for voters in all instances in North Carolina elections.

sections.heading: How it got on the ballot: Session Law 2024-58
sections.by: Session Law 2024-58 (Senate Bill 921), North Carolina General Assembly
paragraphs: SECTION 4. The State Board of Elections shall certify the results of the referendum conducted under Section 3 of this act. If a majority of votes cast on the question are in favor of the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the Secretary of State shall enroll the amendment among the permanent records of that office. If a majority of votes cast on the question are against the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the amendment shall have no effect.

SECTION 5. If the certification from the State Board of Elections under Section 4 of this act reflects that a majority of votes cast on the question are in favor of the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act is effective upon certification.
sections.note: The amendment's own text marks the words it adds and removes by underlining and striking through, which doesn't survive copying, so it isn't shown here. Read it in the session law (linked below).

measures.no_arguments: North Carolina doesn't publish official arguments for or against its constitutional amendments, so there are none to show here. The official summary explanation, the session law and the fiscal note above are the state's official documents on this amendment.

paragraphs: SECTION 3. The State Board of Elections shall certify the results of the referendum conducted under Section 2 of this act. sections.heading: Fiscal note
sections.by: Fiscal Research Division, North Carolina General Assembly: legislative fiscal note, on Senate Bill 1080 (First Edition), May 19, 2026
paragraphs: The bill would require a referendum to be held on a Constitutional Amendment that would decrease the maximum allowable income tax rate, including both personal income tax and corporate income tax, from 7% to 3.5%, beginning on January 1, 2027. This bill is estimated to have no fiscal impact for the following reasons:
The outcome of the ballot measure is unknown.
The personal income tax rate is expected to be below the maximum allowable rate due to the projected impact of exceeding statutory revenue triggers.
The statutory corporate income tax rate is and will be below the maximum allowable rate.
Additional costs associated with administering the election for the referendum are anticipated to be minimal.
sections.note: The note's Fiscal Impact Summary, word for word. It was written on the edition of the bill named above, the latest the General Assembly lists a fiscal note for. The full note, with its analysis and tables, is linked below.

judicial.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election
about: Pursuant to Voter education (N.C.G.S. § 163-278.69), the State Board must publish a Judicial Voter Guide that explains the functions of the appellate courts and the laws concerning the election of appellate judges, the purpose and function of the Public Campaign Fund, and the laws concerning voter registration.

This online guide was created at no cost. In the fall of 2026, a postcard mailer will be mailed to North Carolina households with information about this online guide and a QR code to access it. Funding for the postcard comes from the N.C. Public Campaign Fund, which was created by a $3 check-off designation on the state tax form and a $50 surcharge on annual dues paid by members of the North Carolina State Bar. The fund was repealed in 2013, and that fund is now depleted.
The order of candidates in this guide is the order in which they will appear on the general election ballot for their contest, which is based on a random drawing conducted according to state law.
The information for each candidate was provided by the candidate. Statements by candidates do not express or reflect the opinions of the State Board of Elections.

contests.office: Associate Justice, Supreme Court of North Carolina, Seat 1
contests.guide_heading: NC Supreme Court Associate Justice Seat 1

candidates.name: Anita Earls
details: J.D., Yale Law School, 1988; B.A., Williams College, 1981
Supreme Court of North Carolina, Senior Associate Justice, 2018-present
Southern Coalition for Social Justice, Founder and Executive Director, 2007-2017
UNC Center for Civil Rights, Director of Advocacy, 2003-2007
Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights, Voting Rights Project Director, 2000-2003
U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division, Deputy Assistant Attorney General, 1998-2000
UNC, Duke and University of Maryland, Adjunct Professor

paragraphs: In my nearly 40-year legal career – first as an attorney and now a Justice on the NC Supreme Court – I worked to uphold the Constitution, ensure the justice system treats everyone fairly, and hold those who have broken our laws accountable. After my brother was brutally murdered and his killer never prosecuted, I re-dedicated my life to fighting for justice for victims of crime and ensuring everyone gets their day in Court. I am the only candidate in this race with judicial experience and the only one with experience arguing cases in front of the Supreme Court as an attorney. I believe an independent Court is critically necessary to the balance of powers and absolutely required to maintain a democracy. All North Carolinians should have a fair and independent court that protects their personal freedoms no matter their race, gender or how much money they have in their pockets. Learn more at: www.earls4justice.com.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

candidates.name: Sarah Stevens
details: UNC Greensboro, 1981, B.S. Social Work; Campbell University School of Law, 1986
Private practice attorney for 40 years; State legislator for 17.5 years
Stevens and Brintle; NC General Assembly
14 years as a House Judiciary chair; 6 years as chair of the Court Commission; 40 years of law practice

paragraphs: I possess the knowledge and demeanor to be a Justice. I believe in following the law as written and a strict following of the constitution. I have been the Speaker Pro Tempore of the House and chaired Judiciary committees whose purpose is to review the clarity and the constitutionality of the proposed legislation before it becomes law. I believe in the neutral application of the law.

I am running because my opponent has twice ruled against the constitution on issues of voter identification and redistricting. She has also rewritten the law and disturbed 90 years of common law. I have not been on the bench before but neither had my opponent until the last election.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

contests.office: Judge, North Carolina Court of Appeals, Seat 1

candidates.name: Michael C. Byrne
details: B.A., English, NC State; J.D., Campbell Law

Six years as judge with 400+ decisions. Ten decisions affirmed by Court of Appeals and one by Supreme Court; never reversed by either court. Litigated 20+ cases in NC appeals courts as an attorney as well as appeals briefs for police/ public employee groups. Hundreds of trials including 272 cases in the OAH where I’m now a judge. 30 years combined experience.

paragraphs: My judicial philosophy: “A Fair Judge. For Everyone” - and get the law right.
Endorsed by: NC Police Benevolent Assn, NC Fraternal Order of Police, National Assn of Police Organizations.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

candidates.name: John S. Arrowood
details: Honors Graduate, Hudson High School; B.A., Magna Cum Laude, Catawba College; J.D., University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill
NC Court of Appeals: Law Clerk, Staff Attorney, Staff Director, Judge. Special Superior Court Judge. Attorney in private practice.

paragraphs: No member of or candidate for the Court brings my depth of legal and real-life experiences. I was born in Yancey County and lived there until I was 15 when my parents died just a couple of months apart. I then moved to Caldwell County to live with my brother (a Highway Patrolman) and his family.

Following graduation from UNC-CH, I worked at the Court of Appeals as a law clerk, staff attorney, and staff director. For over 25 years, I was an attorney in private practice doing civil and commercial litigation for individuals and businesses in a wide range of matters. I was also privileged to serve on the NC Banking Commission, the NC Rules Review Commission, the NC Arts Council, and on the NC Railroad board. In Charlotte I have been a trustee of the Mint Museum of Art and on the board of Urban Ministry Center. I am an active member of St. Peter’s Episcopal Church.
As a Court of Appeals Judge for almost 11 years I have written hundreds of decisions.
I am committed to an independent judiciary that upholds the rule of law. I pledge to render equal justice and to protect your constitutional rights.
Learn more at keepjudgearrowood.com.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

contests.office: Judge, North Carolina Court of Appeals, Seat 2

candidates.name: George Cooper Bell
details: Cornell University, B.S., 2000; Regent University School of Law, J.D., 2003

Owned a small business with my wife and law school sweetheart, Hannah Bell, and my focus was criminal law. I was elected to the Superior Court bench in Charlotte, NC, in 2018. As a judge, I have presided over 100 felony jury trials, including cases involving first-degree murder, violent crimes, and habitual felon charges.

paragraphs: My judicial philosophy is simple: I follow the rule of law and administer justice impartially, without prejudice or bias. I believe that people need to be held accountable for their actions. For example, I have kept our streets safe and sentenced numerous violent criminals to life in prison without parole. This election is very critical. Our cities are under attack and there are takeovers almost every weekend creating serious, dangerous situations. As a judge, I have held criminals accountable. I will continue to administer justice to make sure that our local communities are safe from violent crime. I am proud to keep North Carolina families safe, and I am committed to justice. Vote George Bell for judge and "Ring the Bell for Justice." For more information, please visit https://www.JudgeGeorgeBell.com.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

candidates.name: Tobias (Toby) Hampson
details: J.D., Campbell University School of Law, 2002; B.A., American University 1998; NCSSM, 1994.
2004-2007: Attorney, Patterson, Dilthey, Clay, Bryson & Anderson
2002-2004: Law Clerk, N.C. Court of Appeals

paragraphs: It is an honor to serve you as a North Carolina Court of Appeals Judge. I am running for re-election because it is critical we keep Judges with Court of Appeals experience on the bench. I am committed to defending the Rule of Law, upholding your rights, and making sure our judicial system works for the people and not extreme partisan agendas.

On the bench, I have authored hundreds of majority decisions–usually unanimous and often drawing bipartisan support. However, I am also not afraid to dissent when it’s the right thing to do – as I did in Griffin v. N.C. State Bd. of Elections.

Before being elected to the Court in 2018, I focused my career as an attorney representing people and businesses in appeals to the North Carolina Court of Appeals and state Supreme Court. I am certified as an appellate practice specialist by the N.C. State Bar.
I grew up mainly in Moore County. I am a proud product of N.C. public schools. My wife, Kristin, and I have three daughters.
Learn more about me, my endorsements, and the campaign at JudgeTobyHampson.com.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

contests.office: Judge, North Carolina Court of Appeals, Seat 3

candidates.name: Craig Collins
details: I graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 1994 and Villanova University School of Law in 1997.
I am currently a Superior Court Judge.
I am employed by the State of North Carolina.
I was an Assistant District Attorney for 9 years, a private attorney for 9 years, a District Court Judge for 9 years, and I am currently a Superior Court Judge.

paragraphs: North Carolina needs experienced judges who will follow the Constitution and not legislate from the bench. It is vital that we have judges who understand the trial division, where cases are heard prior to arrival at the Court of Appeals. I am the only candidate in my race with both District Court and Superior Court judicial experience, and I also have experience as a prosecutor and private attorney. I have handled the exact types of cases heard by the Court of Appeals throughout my career. Our rights are essential, and I have a proven track record of protecting them daily. Furthermore, community safety is essential, and I have spent a career working to protect our community. I would certainly appreciate your vote. You can learn more about my campaign at www.votecraigcollins.com.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election

candidates.name: Christine Marie Walczyk
details: UNC School of Law, Juris Doctor
Boston College, Carroll School of Management, Bachelor of Science, Finance Concentration, magna cum laude

paragraphs: At 19 years, I am among the longest serving trial judges in our state. I practiced law for over a decade before coming to the bench and have a proven record of safeguarding due process and the rule of law. I have spent my career supporting women in the profession, working to level the playing field for self-represented persons, and fighting for judicial independence. Most importantly, I have tried to act every day with integrity, as a judge that the public can trust.

I am focused on protecting the individual liberties enshrined in our Constitution, promoting equal access to justice, and forging a stronger, independent judiciary that serves the people. I hope to bring experience, integrity, and balance to the Court. As the only woman running for the Court of Appeals in 2026, I fully support a more diverse judiciary that better reflects the population.

I am endorsed by the North Carolina Association of Educators (NCAE), North Carolina Police Benevolent Association (PBA), AFL-CIO of NC, Communications Workers of America NC, Sierra Club NC Chapter, Lillian’s List, Equality NC, Down Home NC, and many former appellate judges who understand what it takes to do this job well.
statement.source: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Judicial Voter Guide: 2026 General Election
